reason: H0 exclusively initializes and drives wuffs_json__decoder and wuffs_aux::DecodeJson, while S1 changes xxhash32 checksum finalization and adds the stateful xxhash64 hasher implementation. Consequently, no input reaches either changed hashing implementation, and the important streaming protocol and boundary-dependent states are unfuzzed.
evidence: H0 enables WUFFS_CONFIG__MODULE__JSON and WUFFS_CONFIG__MODULE__AUX__JSON but no XXHASH32 or XXHASH64 module.
H0's fuzz_simple and fuzz_complex call wuffs_json__decoder__decode_tokens; fuzz_cpp calls wuffs_aux::DecodeJson. No hasher method is invoked.
std/xxhash32/common_xxhash32.wuffs changes hasher.checksum_u32, including placement of this.length_modulo_u32 in both the >=16/overflow and short-input branches.
The new xxhash64.hasher maintains length_modulo_u64, length_overflows_u64, buf_len, buf_data, and v0 through v3 across update calls.
xxhash64.hasher.up processes 32-byte stripes and buffers a 0-to-31-byte remainder, making chunk partitions and lengths around 8, 16, 24, and 32 fuzz-worthy.
xxhash64 exposes both update_u64 and the separate update then checksum_u64 protocol, neither exercised by H0.
recommended_action: Add a hashing harness that enables and instantiates the XXHASH32 and XXHASH64 modules, feeds arbitrary bytes using fuzz-selected chunk boundaries (especially around 4, 8, 16, 24, and 32 bytes), and checks one-shot versus partitioned-update equivalence. Exercise update_u64 as well as update followed by checksum_u64, repeated checksum calls, empty updates, and xxhash32 checksum_u32 across the 16-byte threshold.
